newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady in quiet trading.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil was steady on Tuesday in quiet trading with no new factors emerging to alter the current listless market, traders said.
Traders said supplies were improving with South Korea offering first half September lifting cargoes at around $1.00 per tonne above Singapore spot quotes against bids at about 50 cents premium.
South Korea was seeking to place these cargoes in China due to its comparative freight advantage over Singapore.
Bids from China were around $7.50 per tonne over Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis with offers at close to $10.00 premium.
Traders said Chinese buying interest was limited and they were only picking up bargains.
Supplies from the Middle East had improved recently with several cargoes of mainly higher viscosity material arriving in Singapore last week with the 180-cst now seen tight, they said.
A Kuwaiti cracked 80,000 tonne cargo for end August lifting was sold at discount of $9.00 per tonne below Middle East spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.
Traders said some incremental demand was seen from Indonesia due to the shutdown of the 100,000-barrel-per-day Cilacap crude unit for 35 days beginning August 12.
A 80,000-tonne Middle East cargo was sold earlier to Indonesia to cover this requirement for September arrival, they said.
Also some were expecting further hikes to Indonesian imports for October arrival when the other bigger 200,000-bpd Cilacap crude unit is shutdown for up to three months in early October.
In the spot market, a 20,000 tonne cargo for September 14-18 lifting was offered at $104.50 per tonne, down 50 cents from Monday's selling price.
Trading in the swaps market was also steady with deals seen for September at $104.00 and October at $104.25, brokers said.
September was last quoted unchanged from Monday at $103.75/$104.50 and October at $104.25/$105.00, they said.
The low sulphur waxy residue was under some pressure on talks that Indonesia's September allocation would up to 3.5 million barrels, well over the original estimate of 2.7 million barrels.
Bearish sentiment was also due to the additional allocations of 400,000 barrels for end August lifting on top of the initial 2.7 million allocated in August.
The premiums to Pertamina's formula were assessed at 50 to 70 cents per barrel, fob.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
